items.body:
### Project Name

Microsoft 365 Advanced Analytics

### License

MIT

### Contributor

Sam Betts, Jesus Fernandez Saez

### Existing OSS Project?

Yes

### Source Code URL

https://github.com/pnp/Microsoft365-Analytics-Insights

### Project Homepage URL

_No response_

### Project Transfer Signatories

Sam Betts <sambetts@microsoft.com>
Jesus Fernandez Saez <jesusfer@microsoft.com>

### Description

Open-source .NET engine that collects enhanced Microsoft 365 usage data into a SQL database you own, with Power BI adoption reporting.


### What are you hoping from the foundation

Primarily code-signing infrastructure (we self-manage a cert today) plus the visibility, neutral governance, and CLA/licensing support to grow contributions and collaboration.

### Name

Sam Betts

### Email

sambetts@microsoft.com

### GitHub Profile URL

https://github.com/sambetts

### Committers

Active maintainers with commit/write access (listed in CODEOWNERS), who handle day-to-day commits on behalf of the project:
- Sam Betts — GitHub: sambetts — Microsoft
- Jesus Fernandez — GitHub: jesusfer — [employer]

Because the repository sits under the pnp organization, the PnP organization owners also inherit admin rights on it (not active committers on this project):
- GitHub: erwinvanhunen
- GitHub: waldekmastykarz
- GitHub: patrick-rodgers
- GitHub: pkbullock
- GitHub: Laskewitz
- GitHub: Adam-it
- GitHub: alexc-MSFT
- GitHub: PopWarner
- GitHub: shivvad

### Discord Ids

_No response_

### Governance Model

Proposing changes
All changes are proposed as GitHub pull requests. Contributors fork the repository or create a feature branch and open a PR against the "dev" branch, following CONTRIBUTING.md. For anything beyond a trivial fix, contributors are asked to open
or comment on a GitHub issue first (using our Bug report / Feature request templates) so the approach can be agreed before work starts. Security issues are reported privately via our Security Policy (GitHub private vulnerability reporting), not as public PRs.

Review
Every pull request targets "dev" and is automatically validated by our GitHub Actions workflows (build and unit tests run on each PR). The repository has a CODEOWNERS file, so the project maintainers (currently @sambetts and @jesusfer) are automatically requested as reviewers. Maintainers review each change for correctness, scope, security, performance (the solution is expected to run at large tenant scale) and consistency with the project's coding conventions, and may request changes before it can be merged.

Accepting changes
A change is accepted once CI is green (build + tests pass) and it has approval from a project maintainer / code owner. Maintainers merge approved PRs into "dev" using a merge commit. Changes then flow from "dev" to "main", where the GitHub
Actions release pipeline produces the signed, deployable artifacts published as GitHub Releases. Significant design decisions or disagreements are discussed on the issue/PR and resolved by the maintainers, in consultation with PnP
organization leadership where needed.

Appointing new committers
The project is part of the Microsoft 365 & Power Platform Community (PnP) organization. New committers are identified by a track record of sustained, high-quality contributions and constructive participation in issues and reviews.
When a contributor has demonstrated this, the existing maintainers — together with PnP organization leadership — invite them to become a maintainer, grant write access, and add them to CODEOWNERS as appropriate. Write/admin access is managed
through the pnp GitHub organization.

### CLA

- [ ] If already an OSS project, was a Contribution License Agreement in place for contributions accepted?

### How does the project check who has signed one?

_No response_

### CLA Notification Alias

_No response_

### Select the Project Transfer Agreement model

Contribution

### Repository Layout

**Current state**
The public GitHub repo (pnp/Microsoft365-Analytics-Insights) is already the single upstream / "master" for the project - there is no separate internal source of truth. The core development team uses the same process as external contributors: feature branch or fork -> pull request against the "dev" branch -> CI (build + unit tests) -> CODEOWNERS review -> merge. We will keep this model after joining.

**Already in place**
- Root README.md, MIT LICENSE, .gitignore
- CONTRIBUTING.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (adopting the .NET Foundation Code of
  Conduct), SECURITY.md
- Issue templates (bug / feature), pull request template, CODEOWNERS
- Source under /src (AnalyticsEngine + SPO), Power BI assets under /reports,
  tests under src/AnalyticsEngine/Tests.*

**Changes we would make as part of joining**
1. LICENSE / copyright: update the copyright statement at the top of LICENSE to "Copyright (c) .NET Foundation and Contributors. All Rights Reserved" (keeping the MIT terms), per the Project Assignment Agreement and copyright guidance. (Currently it reads "Copyright (c) 2024 Microsoft 365 & Power Platform Community".)
2. File headers: add the standard .NET Foundation source-file header ("// Licensed to the .NET Foundation under one or more agreements. ...") to our source files, which currently have none.
3. CLA: enable the .NET Foundation CLA bot and update CONTRIBUTING.md to cover signing the CLA on a first pull request.
4. Add a .gitattributes for line-ending normalization (not present today).
5. Add NOTICE.md / ThirdPartyNotices.txt surfacing the third-party components we bundle/depend on and their licenses.
6. (Optional) Make documentation PR-reviewable by mirroring our GitHub wiki into a "Documentation/" folder or docs repo, per the guidance's preference for a docs folder over a wiki. We currently maintain docs in the GitHub wiki.

We do not anticipate restructuring the source tree itself; it already follows /src + /reports with tests alongside the solution.

### Eligibility Criteria

- [x] The project is built on the .NET platform and/or creates value within the .NET ecosystem.
- [x] The project produces source code for distribution to the public at no charge.
- [x] The project's code is easily discoverable and publicly accessible (preferably on GitHub).
- [x] The project contains a build script that can produce deployable artifacts that are identical to the official deployable artifacts, with the exception of code signing (Exception may be granted for strong name keys, though strongly encouraged to be committed. Exception relies on OSS signing being in the build script for public builds).
- [x] When applicable, project must use reproducible build settings in its toolchain.
- [ ] The project uses [Source Link.](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/library-guidance/sourcelink)
- [x] The project uses either embedded PDBs or publish symbol packages to NuGet (if applicable).
- [x] The project code signs their artifacts as appropriate.
- [x] The project organization has 2FA enabled. Requiring 2FA must be done as part of onboarding if not already enabled.
- [x] Libraries that are mandatory dependencies of the project are offered under a standard, permissive open source license which has been approved by the .NET Foundation (exceptions include a dependency that is required by the target platform where no alternative open source dependency is available such as the .NET Framework or a hardware specific library).
- [x] Committers are bound by a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) and/or are willing to embrace the .NET Foundation's CLA when the project becomes a Member.
- [x] The copyright ownership of everything that the project produces is clearly defined and documented.
- [x] The project has a public issue tracker where the status of any defect can be easily obtained.
- [x] The project has a published Security Policy.
- [x] The project has a home page which provides high level information about its status and purpose.
- [x] The project has a public communication channel where community members can engage with maintainers.
- [x] The project has a publicly available location where members can review and contribute to documentation.

### Describe why you are applying for Project Membership.

We are applying to give the project a neutral, long-term home with the Foundation's governance and credibility, and to gain code-signing infrastructure, CLA/licensing support, and the visibility to grow our contributor community - in line with the Foundation's mission to strengthen the .NET ecosystem through openly developed software.

### Infrastructure Requirements Summary

**Build servers**
All CI/CD runs on GitHub Actions using GitHub-hosted runners - windows-latest for the .NET / MSBuild builds and installer signing, and ubuntu-latest for the TypeScript SharePoint "AI Tracker" build and the release step. Builds trigger on
push to main/dev and publish versioned artifacts as GitHub Releases. We do not need any dedicated or self-hosted build servers; the existing GitHub Actions setup is sufficient.

**Web / service hosting**
The product itself is not a hosted service - each customer deploys it into their own Azure subscription (App Service web jobs + an admin web app, Azure SQL, Redis, and optional Service Bus / Cognitive Services / Automation). So there is no
central application hosting the Foundation needs to provide. The public surfaces are the GitHub repository, the GitHub wiki (documentation), and GitHub Releases (artifact distribution).

We do operate two small ancillary endpoints today, in a maintainer-controlled Azure subscription:
 - An Azure Blob Storage container that hosts the installer's downloadable
   software payloads (referenced by the installer at runtime).
 - An optional, anonymous usage-telemetry/stats Web API (the src/TelemetryService
   component) that importer jobs can post aggregate stats to; it is skipped
   entirely if an operator leaves it unconfigured.
These are modest and can remain maintainer-operated. We're open to discussing whether the Foundation would prefer them hosted/funded differently.

**SSL / Authenticode code signing**
Code signing is our main infrastructure ask. The Windows installer (AnalyticsInstaller.exe) is Authenticode-signed during the GitHub Actions release build, currently using a self-managed PFX certificate stored as GitHub secrets and timestamped via DigiCert. We would like to move to the Foundation's code-signing service so releases are signed under a Foundation-backed certificate and we no longer manage/renew the certificate or store its secret ourselves.

We do not require any SSL/TLS certificates from the Foundation: there is no project-run public website, and customer deployments use their own Azure TLS certificates. (The two ancillary endpoints above already terminate TLS in our
existing Azure setup.)

### Additional Notes

**General notes**
This project is maintained as part of the Microsoft 365 & Power Platform Community (PnP) and developed in the open on GitHub (pnp/Microsoft365-Analytics-Insights), which is the single source of truth; releases are published as signed GitHub Releases. Ahead of this application we added a Code of Conduct (the .NET Foundation CoC), SECURITY.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, enabled GitHub Discussions and private vulnerability reporting, and set the repo home page to the wiki.

**Similar projects and how we differ**
The closest alternatives are Microsoft's own offerings — the built-in Microsoft 365 usage reports / admin center, the Power BI "Microsoft 365 usage analytics" content pack, Viva Insights (formerly Workplace Analytics), and Microsoft Graph Data Connect (MGDC) — plus commercial third-party M365/SharePoint analytics products (e.g. CardioLog, Rencore, AvePoint). We differ in a few key ways:

- **Open source and self-hosted:** it runs entirely inside the customer's own Azure tenant and writes to a SQL database the customer owns — no SaaS, no per-seat fee, and data never leaves their compliance boundary.
- **Ownable, long-term history:** queryable detail instead of the rolling 7–180 day, pre-aggregated, often de-identified built-in reports.
- **One joined schema across workloads** (SharePoint, Teams/calls, Outlook, OneDrive, Viva Engage, Copilot, Power Platform) at page/click/session, call, message and Copilot-interaction granularity, with users enriched by department, manager, title and licensed SKU.
- **Turnkey:** a deployable engine + installer + ready-made Power BI reports, rather than a raw data-export pipeline (like MGDC) that requires the customer to build their own data engineering.

**Areas where we may need early help / things to discuss**
1. **Code signing:** guidance on moving our GitHub Actions release pipeline from a self-managed Authenticode PFX to the Foundation's code-signing service, for a classic .NET Framework WinForms installer.
2. **Copyright / CLA and Microsoft employees:** several maintainers are Microsoft employees contributing as part of PnP. We'd welcome guidance on the Project Assignment Agreement, applying Foundation copyright + file headers across the existing codebase, and how the .NET Foundation CLA interacts with Microsoft's corporate CLA coverage.
3. **Trademark / naming:** the project and repo names reference "Microsoft 365" (a Microsoft trademark). As a Microsoft-sponsored community (PnP) project we believe this is supported, but we'd like to confirm naming/branding guidance.
4. **Ancillary services:** a small Azure Blob download container and an optional telemetry/stats API currently run in a maintainer-controlled Azure subscription; we'd like to agree how these are owned/funded going forward.
5. **Documentation:** our docs live in the GitHub wiki; if the Foundation prefers a PR-reviewable docs folder/repo, we'd welcome help planning that migration.
6. **Maintainer base / bus factor:** there are currently two active code owners; growing the contributor and maintainer base is one of our goals in joining.

items.title: feat(context): add native source records and evidence-backed atoms
items.body:
> **Current naming/source contract, 23 October 2026:** this is The Onlinesourdough Method (OSM). Use Context Architecture for the data/context design; AI Operating Model keeps its name. Production naming is delivered in [PR80](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/pull/80), released v0.30.0. The pre-existing Setup feature preview is preserved separately in [PR81](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/pull/81), not promoted to production. Current implementation paths below use `osm` / `osm-*`; [#76](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/76) tracks remaining rollout. All functional requirements and holds remain; naming delivery does not mean this feature has shipped.

## Problem and result

OSM already has durable Memory metadata and decision reasons. What is missing is a distinct, queryable place for selected session/meeting evidence and derived atoms before they become trusted durable knowledge. Add the smallest native record model that makes those records useful to people and agents, preserving existing Memory and Docs semantics.

Parent: [#68](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/68). Contract dependency: [#69](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/69). Provides the record contract to [#71](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/71), [#72](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/72) and [#73](https://github.com/onlinesourdough/OSM-plugin/issues/73).

## Default Notion shape

- Reuse an appropriate existing Docs/Meetings destination for captured source records. A new default may use Docs with its existing `Type = Source` view for sessions; meeting notes keep the resolved Meetings destination. Do not create a new Sessions database merely to obtain another view.
- When the selected capture workflow needs atoms and no suitable store exists, create **one small Atoms database** linked to its source records. An existing compatible database/view can implement the same role. This is not a new native Notion `database_type`, and not a replacement or second copy of Memory.
- Keep the source map at source-system/scope level; a captured document is an individual session/meeting. Define the link between those two identities so hundreds of sessions do not become hundreds of dashboard systems.
- Keep source evidence at its owning system when durable accessible references suffice. Store a sanitized source excerpt/export only when that retention is selected. Summaries and atoms link to the exact evidence location; missing full evidence is an explicit limit.

## Minimal semantic contract

Use existing fields with matching meaning; do not force identical names or widen every database. Put searchable/filterable values in native properties, richer provenance/rationale in the page body. Define the default physical schema and views in the Context-owned reference before creation.

| Record | Required meaning | Native representation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source record | Stable origin identity scoped to provider/account; route; source URL/export reference; original event date if known; capture time; observed source revision if available; summary; completeness/access state | Existing Docs/Meetings title, Key, Source/Date where semantically compatible; add only missing properties needed by the selected workflow, with evidence/provenance in body |
| Atom | One independently useful claim; stable key; origin relation plus evidence locator; kind; original date inherited/recorded; topic/project where useful; state | Small Atoms database: descriptive title/claim, Key, Source relation, Kind, Status and relevant date/topic properties; body holds exact evidence, uncertainty, derivation and reason |
| Promotion | Durable Memory/Doc/Skill destination and relationship to originating evidence | Link/reference to the actual owning record; no parallel live task or repeated profile |

Define two separate identities: a stable source-item Key (provider/account/route + original item ID) and an observed revision/processed revision. An edit is not an unrelated new source. Atom Keys identify their source/revision and logical claim; rerunning extraction first reconciles existing claims rather than treating a differently worded summary as new knowledge. Native Created time can represent initial capture only when that meaning holds; migration must preserve the original captured time separately.

Define minimal lifecycle meanings, mapped to existing compatible properties: active, changed/incomplete, unavailable (unconfirmed access/fetch failure), confirmed deleted/revoked, and forgotten by the owner. Apply recorded exclusions before collection. Retain only the minimal non-content identity/exclusion marker needed to prevent reimport after forgetting, subject to the owner's deletion policy; never keep the forgotten claim in a tombstone. Where a marker itself must be removed, the route must be excluded/disabled or an equivalent upstream exclusion must prevent reimport.

Keep explicit derivation links from atom to evidence and from atom to promoted destinations. Prefer native relation(s) to the actual destination types, or stable URLs plus an indexed relation where necessary; do not assume one Notion relation can target arbitrary databases. Existing Memory schema remains intact. A dependent claim with no remaining valid evidence is marked for review under the standing write policy and excluded from current answers pending resolution; independent corroboration is evaluated rather than deleted. A bad extraction batch can be identified by its receipt/route and extraction time and retracted without deleting original evidence or later human corrections.

An atom can be a reported fact, decision, constraint, lesson, or verified fix. Mark extraction vs human/source confirmation explicitly. Do not invent confidence percentages, reasons, authors or dates. Preserve the exact original error/command when useful and safely scoped; an attempted command is not a proven fix.

Memory's native `Source` remains the creating client and `Last updated by` the editing client; original evidence stays separate. Do not conflate Docs `Source`/`Date` with Memory's native meanings. `Imported`/capture time is not source date or proof of currency. Existing Decision `Reason and evidence` content remains.

Provide useful Recent, Needs review and By source/project views over the same records, not duplicated databases. Space/filters organize content but grant no access. Derived records must not be shared more broadly than the approved source/retention policy allows.

## Source owners and acceptance

Context's `references/home-contract.md`, `references/notion/schema-and-templates.md`, `references/notion/operating.md` and provider equivalents own the schema. This issue also owns the parent-listed deliberate capture-policy update; Capture and Maintain Context link to it. Extend existing templates and migration/recovery procedures only where needed. Optional file-home records do not require an `AIOS_FORMAT` change unless readers actually need a new mandatory format; preserve unknown files under the existing contract.

- [ ] Create a synthetic source record and related atoms through the actual supported Notion connection; property-filter/view/search finds a useful atom and follows it to evidence without loading the full transcript.
- [ ] Reuse a populated compatible Docs/Meetings/Memory setup without renaming native semantics or changing existing IDs/permissions/content. Unchanged replay creates no new database or atom.
- [ ] Old source imported today retains its old/unknown source date; explicit decision, uncertain statement and failed attempt remain distinguishable. A planted secret is absent from persisted excerpts, atoms and summaries.
- [ ] Corrected/superseded/unavailable evidence can be represented and excluded from ordinary current answers without erasing useful history. Record migration/additive setup has readback and a bounded recovery path.
- [ ] The same roles work in the existing managed-file home using ordinary files/frontmatter or an existing index. No mandatory external index or new general storage abstraction is introduced.
- [ ] Verify a new write by direct ID/property query even while ordinary search indexing lags. Preserve evidence/exclusion markers and original capture times across an authorized home move. A forgotten record is not recreated by the next intake; a bad batch is recoverable without erasing later owner edits.

This issue does not claim every existing Memory row is complete, does not import owner data, and does not redesign all Notion databases. Native capability checks precede claiming support on a specific plan.

items.title: Spec: Phase 1 hosted instances
items.body:
## Problem Statement

Job-seeking software engineers will not set up Job Finder themselves. Asking them for Jina, OpenRouter, and Typesafe accounts is enough to kill the attempt, even when they need a job and even when the Operator offers to walk them through it. The public repo stays useful for the Operator. It is not how an Owner starts.

The Operator needs a way to stand up a private instance, pay the providers, sit through the first Reviews, see spend and whether the Owner is actually reviewing, pause idle discovery so money is not burned, and look at traces and logs without building a SaaS.

## Solution

Phase 1 is a Hosted instance per Owner, run by the Operator.

The Owner gets a URL, a password, and a Setup session. Provider keys never belong to the Owner. The Operator pays Jina, OpenRouter, and Typesafe. The product is free. There is no public cap. Each instance already has a monthly budget so one Owner cannot torch the bill overnight.

The public offer is a personal page: first person, MIT, free, book a Setup session. Not a company. Not self-serve BYOK. Not employer-side software.

The Operator may see Queue data (listings shown, Review decisions, notes) and may use it to improve the product and to learn whether the product is useful. The Operator does not publish an Owner's companies or notes. Job Finder never collects application form answers or recruiter conversations.

Discovery Idle-pauses when an Owner has recorded no Review for 5 days. Data stays. Owner and Operator both see that it paused. The Operator can resume it.

Observability for phase 1: Langfuse Cloud (paid, managed) for LLM traces and evals. Better Stack (cloud) for logs, traces, and heartbeats. Instance Postgres for spend and last Review. No ClickStack. No PostHog. No Plausible. No Grafana. No cross-instance Operator list until there are 5 or more Owners.

During the Setup session the Owner Reviews in the browser. The Operator runs the Teaching loop (Curation, Manifest, Release target) over MCP.

This spec is the product source for phase 1. It does not replace roadmap mauricedesaxe/job-finder#156. It changes what mauricedesaxe/job-finder#157 means: self-serve Compose is no longer the phase-1 offer. Pieces of mauricedesaxe/job-finder#157 that still matter (bounded test search, budget, operations home) stay useful inside a Hosted instance.

## User Stories

1. As an Owner, I want a URL and a password, so that I never install Docker or create provider accounts.
2. As an Owner, I want a live Setup session with the Operator, so that the search is shaped for me before I am left alone.
3. As an Owner, I want to Review jobs in the browser during that session, so that I can say what I like and why.
4. As an Owner, I want later runs to get better after those Reviews, so that I trust the queue.
5. As an Owner, I want a hard monthly spend cap on my instance, so that the Operator's bill cannot explode on my search.
6. As an Owner, I want to see that discovery paused because I have not Reviewed in 5 days, so that I know why new jobs stopped appearing.
7. As an Owner, I want the Operator to be able to resume discovery, so that I can come back without losing my queue.
8. As an Owner, I want my queue private to my instance, so that other Owners cannot see my jobs or notes.
9. As an Owner, I want to know the Operator can see my queue, so that the exchange is honest.
10. As an Owner, I want application answers and recruiter talk to stay out of this product, so that I am not handing over my whole job search.
11. As an Owner, I want to book a Setup session from a public page, so that I do not have to clone a repo.
12. As an Owner, I want the page to say the product is free and self-hosted-for-me, not a company, so that I am not sold a SaaS I did not ask for.
13. As an Operator, I want to clone one private stack per Owner, so that I can offer Hosted instances this month without a multi-tenant rewrite.
14. As an Operator, I want provider keys to live only on my side, so that Owners never become Operators.
15. As an Operator, I want to pay Jina, OpenRouter, and Typesafe myself, so that signups are not the onboarding.
16. As an Operator, I want each instance's recorded model spend on `/operations`, so that I know who is costing money.
17. As an Operator, I want last Review time and days idle on `/operations`, so that I can see whether the Owner is using the queue.
18. As an Operator, I want discovery to Idle-pause after 5 days with no Review, so that I do not pay for scoring nobody reads.
19. As an Operator, I want to pause and resume schedules by hand on `/operations`, so that I can override the Idle pause.
20. As an Operator, I want Langfuse Cloud traces for each instance, so that I can debug evaluations without self-hosting Langfuse.
21. As an Operator, I want Better Stack logs, traces, and heartbeats per instance, so that I notice when a pipeline dies.
22. As an Operator, I want Queue data, so that I can corroborate Setup-session interviews with what they actually pursue and reject.
23. As an Operator, I want to reuse Queue data in aggregate to improve default criteria, so that the next Owner starts closer to a good search.
24. As an Operator, I do not want to quote an Owner's companies or notes in public, so that the privacy exchange holds.
25. As an Operator, I want the GitHub repo to stay public, so that the software remains inspectable, without sending civilians there to install it.
26. As an Operator, I want MCP for Curation and Release-target promotion, so that I can finish the Teaching loop after the Owner has labeled jobs.
27. As an Operator, I do not want Owners to configure MCP on day one, so that the Setup session does not add another install.
28. As an Operator, I want a bounded test search on a new instance, so that the first session produces real jobs instead of stalling onboarding.
29. As an Operator, I want defaults blanked or replaced during the Setup session, so that an Owner does not inherit the Operator's Europe / $130k search.
30. As an Operator, I do not want a cross-instance console until 5 or more Owners, so that we do not build a control plane for a handful of URLs.
31. As an Operator, I want to live in each instance's `/operations` until then, so that cost and idle are visible without a new product.
32. As a visitor to the public page, I want a short first-person pitch, a demo, and a booking link, so that I can talk to the Operator instead of bouncing on clone instructions.
33. As a visitor, I do not want pricing, waitlists, or employer-side vapor, so that the page matches what exists.

## Implementation Decisions

- Keep one process and one Postgres per Hosted instance. Do not introduce multi-tenant tenancy, shared databases, or a SaaS account table.
- Provisioning an instance is an Operator runbook (clone the existing Compose or Railway stack, Operator keys, unique URL, bootstrap token, budget). It is not an in-app signup flow.
- Extend the existing operations snapshot with last Review at and days since last Review. Surface both on `/operations`. Prefer this over a new analytics product.
- Idle pause is a control-plane change to discovery: if no Review has been recorded for 5 days, stop admitting scheduled discovery. Keep data. Show a banner to the Owner (review or home) and to the Operator (`/operations`). Resume is the existing schedule-resume control, plus clearing the idle flag.
- Unsure does not count as a Review for idle. Only pursue or reject resets the 5-day clock.
- Spend on `/operations` stays recorded model spend from `model_call_attempts`. Do not block phase 1 on splitting Jina vs OpenRouter vs Typesafe.
- Point Langfuse projection at Langfuse Cloud with per-instance project keys. Do not add a self-hosted Langfuse compose to the app stack.
- Keep Better Stack heartbeat URLs per instance. Send logs and traces to Better Stack. Do not add ClickStack, PostHog, Plausible, or Grafana to the instance compose.
- Teaching loop: Owner Reviews in the existing review UI. Operator uses the existing MCP tools for Curation, Manifest, compare, and Release-target activate. Do not build browser Curation in this spec.
- Public page is a static personal page with calendar CTA, demo link, and GitHub as a secondary link. It is not served as a new authenticated app surface.
- mauricedesaxe/job-finder#157 remains open for Hosted-instance first-run holes that still apply (especially bounded test search completing onboarding). Its acceptance of "a non-technical owner deploys without the Operator" is not phase-1 scope.
- No cross-instance Operator list in this spec.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior, not internals. Prefer existing contract and review-app tests over new frameworks.
- Idle pause: given a last pursue/reject older than 5 days, scheduled discovery is not admitted; after a new pursue or reject, it is admitted again. Unsure does not reset. Resume from operations leaves discovery runnable.
- Operations snapshot: last Review at and days idle match the latest pursue/reject, not unsure, and render on `/operations`.
- Onboarding: a fresh Hosted instance can reach a completed first-run including a bounded test search (the mauricedesaxe/job-finder#157 hole), without editing source.
- Prior art: `contracts/test_operations.py`, `contracts/test_postgres_authority.py` (execution budget admission), `job_finder/review/test_app.py`, `job_finder/test_execution_budget.py`.
- Do not require live Langfuse Cloud or Better Stack in unit tests. Heartbeat and Langfuse URLs stay configuration. Projection and heartbeat behavior already have isolated tests.

## Out of Scope

- Multi-tenant SaaS, billing Owners, pass-through API invoices.
- Self-serve BYOK as the marketed install path.
- Using Claude / ChatGPT / Cursor subscriptions as the batch LLM backend.
- Browser Curation, in-app Teaching loop, or hiding MCP from the Operator.
- Cross-instance Operator console.
- ClickStack, PostHog, Plausible, Grafana, self-hosted Langfuse.
- Publishing Queue data. Application forms. Recruiter conversations. Relationship CRM (#45).
- Employer-side screening software.
- One-click Railway for strangers.

## Further Notes

GitHub is the product-intent tracker for this spec. Beads stays empty until this body is approved. Do not apply `ready-for-agent` until a trusted product approver hashes the published body.

Railway will not run a second observability database for $10. That is why ClickStack was dropped. Better Stack Cloud and Langfuse Cloud are the paid ops cost besides Jina, OpenRouter, and Typesafe.

The public GitHub repo remains the source the Operator deploys. README may still document Compose. The landing page must not send civilians into that README as the start.

items.title: Cost telemetry pipeline is dark end-to-end: no per-customer D1s, no usage-API access, org-level attribution
items.body:
Found by the Review 5 unit-economics stress test (2026-07-03). The cost pipeline (ADR 0023 / cost-telemetry + cost-anomaly workers) is not producing data at any link of the chain:

1. **No per-customer D1 databases exist.** \`wrangler d1 list\` shows none, and \`customer_configs.connectors_json.per_customer_d1_database_id\` is NULL for both live seats — so the daily ingest cron skips 100% of customers by design (\`workers/cost-telemetry/src/index.ts:44-72\`). \`cost_telemetry\` and \`captain_time_events\` (the only labor instrumentation) have nowhere to write. \`cost_anomaly_alerts\` is empty.
2. **The Anthropic usage API rejects our key.** \`/v1/organizations/usage_report/messages\` requires an Admin API key; the \`/ss\` vault has only the runtime \`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\` (verified: \`authentication_error\`). Even with D1s provisioned, ingest 401s. Needs an \`ANTHROPIC_ADMIN_KEY\` provisioned and the worker secret set.
3. **Attribution is org-level.** \`fetchDailyUsage()\` calls the usage API with one org key and writes the same org-wide totals into *each* customer's DB — per-seat COGS cannot be isolated. Fix direction: per-customer Anthropic workspaces (workspace_id grouping on the usage API) or per-seat keys.
4. 15 of the 17 spec'd drivers (Fly, D1, R2, Vectorize, AgentMail, ...) are phase-2 stubs — known/accepted, listed for completeness.

**Decision needed before build:** provision per-customer D1s + admin key + workspace attribution as designed, or re-point v1 at a single central table (simpler, still ADR 0009-compliant since it holds SMD-side billing metadata, not customer data). Related: the COGS/MRR kill gate (>40% two consecutive months) is unarmed both because of this and because no Operator price is authored (#1659).

The opus-4-8 zero-costing bug found in the same review was fixed in #1658.

items.title: As a Service, DB schema?
items.body:
<!-- agentloop:waitstate -->
**Current state:** 💤 waiting for human
<!-- /agentloop:waitstate -->

<!-- agentloop:ui-link -->
[Open in AgentLoop UI](https://agentloop.thomas-guettler.de/#/issues/otelhouse/47)
<!-- /agentloop:ui-link -->

<!-- agentloop:plan -->
## Questions

1. How many tenants do you expect (tens, hundreds, thousands)? Above ~1k databases ClickHouse metadata starts to hurt and Option B (shared tables + row policies) becomes more attractive than Option A (database-per-tenant).
2. Do customers bring their own Grafana, or do you host Grafana for them? Hosted Grafana lets us add a second auth layer; BYO Grafana means the ClickHouse credential **is** the only boundary.
3. Per-tenant retention/quotas — uniform across all tenants, or sold as tiers? Determines whether TTL is baked into DDL or made overridable per tenant.
4. Is the Collector hosted by you or by the customer? If customer-hosted, the ingest-token rotation story needs to be designed in v1, not deferred.
5. Tenant-id format and naming rules — confirm short slug (`[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,30}`) with a reserved-name list (`default`, `system`, `test`, `tenant_admin`)?
6. Is the existing single-tenant `test:test` setup kept as a dev/CI mode, or replaced entirely by a "tenant `test`" in the new model? Affects whether the Dagger pipeline grows a tenancy layer or stays as-is.
7. Scope of this issue: do you want the full v1 (provisioning tool + Collector routing + Dagger isolation test + docs), or just a written design doc this round? The previous code attempt failed and was escalated — knowing whether to ship code or just docs would unblock the next run.

## Goal

Run otelhouse as a multi-tenant service where each customer connects their own Grafana directly to ClickHouse and can only see their own traces, logs, and metrics — with zero risk of cross-tenant reads.

## Constraints driving the design

- Customers connect Grafana **directly** to ClickHouse → the isolation boundary must live inside ClickHouse, not in an app-layer proxy.
- otelhouse today is a Dagger test harness with one shared ClickHouse user (`test:test`) writing to a single `test` database with the upstream `clickhouseexporter` schemas (`otel_traces`, `otel_logs`, `otel_metrics_*`). No tenancy primitives exist yet (see README.md and ci/main.go:42-49).
- Schemas are produced by the upstream Collector exporter, not by us — any tenant marker has to be modelled as an OTel resource attribute or a database boundary, not a custom DDL change to the `otel_*` tables.

## Options considered

**A. Database-per-tenant (recommended)**
One ClickHouse database per customer (`tenant_<id>`), each with its own `otel_traces` / `otel_logs` / `otel_metrics_*` set. One ClickHouse user per customer with `GRANT SELECT ON tenant_<id>.*` only. Grafana datasource per customer points at that user.

- Pros: hardest isolation boundary ClickHouse offers; no row-policy escape hatches; per-tenant retention/TTL/quota knobs; easy to drop a tenant (`DROP DATABASE`).
- Cons: N×7 tables; Collector needs one exporter (or routing pipeline) per tenant; provisioning automation required.

**B. Shared tables + row policies**
Single set of tables, add a `tenant_id` materialized column derived from `ResourceAttributes['tenant.id']`. One ClickHouse user per customer with a row policy on every table.

- Pros: single schema, simpler ingest, lower object count.
- Cons: relies on row policies being correct on every query path Grafana issues; any new table added by a Collector upgrade must get a matching policy or it leaks; harder to defend in a security review.

**C. Cluster-per-tenant** — out of scope for v1; revisit only if a customer demands physical isolation.

**Recommendation: Option A.** "Customer A cannot read customer B" is easier to defend behind a `GRANT` boundary than behind row policies layered over shared tables.

## Implementation plan (Option A)

1. **Tenant provisioning tool (`cmd/tenantctl` or Dagger function)**
   Given a tenant id, the tool runs against ClickHouse as the admin user and:
   - `CREATE DATABASE tenant_<id>`
   - `CREATE USER tenant_<id>_ro IDENTIFIED BY '<generated>'` + `GRANT SELECT ON tenant_<id>.* TO tenant_<id>_ro` (Grafana side — read-only)
   - `CREATE USER tenant_<id>_ingest IDENTIFIED BY '<generated>'` + `GRANT INSERT, CREATE TABLE ON tenant_<id>.* TO tenant_<id>_ingest` (Collector side — lets `create_schema: true` auto-build the `otel_*` tables on first write)
   - Apply the hardened settings profile (step 4) to both users.
   - Emit both credentials + the ingest endpoint to stdout (operator pipes into their secret store).
   - A matching `tenantctl delete <id>` performs `DROP USER` × 2 then `DROP DATABASE tenant_<id> SYNC`.

2. **Ingestion routing**
   Each tenant gets its own OTLP endpoint at the Collector, authenticated with a per-tenant token.
   - **Default (≤ ~50 tenants):** one receiver + one `clickhouse/<tenant>` exporter per tenant in the Collector config, with `database: tenant_<id>` and the ingest user's creds. Generated by `tenantctl` as a config fragment included from the main Collector config.
   - **Scale path:** single OTLP receiver + a `routing` processor keyed on the bearer token or `tenant.id` resource attribute, fanning out to N exporters. Switch when the per-tenant-pipeline config gets unwieldy.
   - Hard rule: writes without a valid tenant credential are rejected. No "default" database fallback.

3. **Grafana wiring**
   - Document the exact datasource JSON for `grafana-clickhouse-datasource`: host, port (9440 / TLS), `username: tenant_<id>_ro`, `defaultDatabase: tenant_<id>`, `secureJsonData.password`.
   - Mark the datasource read-only in Grafana so the UI doesn't offer write actions.
   - Cross-database queries (`FROM tenant_other.otel_traces`) must fail with "Not enough privileges" thanks to the `GRANT`, not return empty rows — verified in tests (step 5).

4. **Defense-in-depth ClickHouse settings**
   Define a `tenant` settings profile applied to all `tenant_*_ro` users:
   - `readonly = 2` (allows `SET` so Grafana works, forbids writes/DDL).
   - `access_management = 0`.
   - `max_concurrent_queries_for_user`, `max_memory_usage_for_user`, `max_execution_time` set to sane defaults.
   - Deny external-data functions (`remote`, `remoteSecure`, `url`, `file`, `s3`, `s3Cluster`, `mysql`, `postgresql`, `mongodb`, `cluster`, `clusterAllReplicas`) via the profile's function restrictions so a compromised tenant credential can't exfiltrate by opening a second connection.
   - Query log stays in `system.query_log`, queryable only by the admin user.

5. **Dagger integration test for isolation**
   New test in the pipeline that:
   - Calls `tenantctl create a` and `tenantctl create b`.
   - Ingests one identifiable span/log into each tenant via the Collector.
   - Asserts:
     - `tenant_a_ro` selecting from `tenant_a.otel_traces` returns its row.
     - `tenant_a_ro` selecting from `tenant_b.otel_traces` → error (not empty result).
     - `tenant_a_ro` calling `remote(...)`, `url(...)`, `file(...)`, `s3(...)` → error.
     - `tenant_a_ro` attempting `INSERT` / `CREATE TABLE` → error.
     - `tenant_a_ingest` attempting `SELECT` → error.
   - This becomes the regression net for every Collector / ClickHouse upgrade.

6. **Docs**
   - New `docs/multi-tenancy.md`: threat model ("Grafana is untrusted from our side; the tenant credential is the only boundary"), provisioning flow, datasource template, explicit non-goals (no PII redaction, no cost attribution, no per-tenant encryption keys in v1).
   - Update `README.md` to link to it and to flag that the existing `test:test` single-tenant setup is dev/CI-only.

## Out of scope for this issue

- Billing / cost attribution per tenant.
- A self-service signup UI (operator runs `tenantctl` for now).
- Cross-tenant aggregate dashboards for the operator (separate issue).
- Migrating an existing single-tenant deployment's data into the new layout.

<!-- /agentloop:plan -->

When I want to use otelhouse in a product for customers, I need to be sure consumer A can't read data from customer B.

I plan to super  customers connecting grafana to Clickhouse..

items.title: Replace VNPay with PayOS subscription payment (backend)

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Ticket is scoped and ready to be picked up by an agent

items.body:
## Problem Statement

FinViet's backend subscription payment layer is built entirely around VNPay, which the team cannot use because business registration was never completed. The VNPay client, IPN handler, hash helper, renewal scheduler, and every VNPay-specific column on the `payments` table are dead infrastructure. There is no working path for a customer's payment to reach the backend and activate a subscription.

## Solution

Replace VNPay with PayOS (payos.vn) as the payment provider. PayOS accepts individual registration, supports VietQR bank transfer, provides a .NET SDK (`Net.payOS`), and verifies payments via webhook with checksum signatures. The backend creates PayOS payment orders, receives webhook confirmations, and applies the result through the same subscription-activation pipeline the VNPay integration used - just with provider-neutral parameters instead of VNPay-specific ones.

## User Stories

1. As a mobile app, I want to call `POST /api/subscriptions/create-payment` with a plan ID and receive a QR code data string, order code, amount, and expiry timestamp, so that I can render the VietQR code in-app for the customer to scan.
2. As a mobile app, I want to poll `GET /api/subscriptions/payment-status/{orderCode}` and receive a status of pending, succeeded, failed, or expired, so that I can show the customer real-time payment confirmation.
3. As a mobile app, I want to call `GET /api/subscriptions/plans` and receive the list of active plans with their names, prices, billing intervals, and features, so that I can display the plan picker.
4. As a mobile app, I want to call `GET /api/subscriptions/current` and receive the customer's active subscription (plan name, status, expiry date, locked price) or null, so that I can show their current plan status.
5. As PayOS, I want to POST a webhook to `POST /api/webhooks/payos` with a signed payload containing the order code and payment status, so that the backend can mark the payment as succeeded or failed.
6. As a backend operator, I want every incoming PayOS webhook verified against the checksumKey before any state change, so that forged payment confirmations are rejected.
7. As a backend operator, I want the payment result service to be idempotent (a duplicate webhook for an already-resolved payment is a no-op), so that PayOS retries never create duplicate subscriptions.
8. As a backend operator, I want each PayOS order to carry a unique numeric order code derived from the payment record, so that the webhook can be matched to the correct payment row.
9. As a backend operator, I want PayOS credentials stored as environment variables (`PayOS__ClientId`, `PayOS__ApiKey`, `PayOS__ChecksumKey`), never in committed config files, so that secrets stay out of the repository.
10. As a customer subscribing for the first time, I want a successful payment to create a new `CustomerSubscription` row with status `active`, the plan's billing interval determining the next billing date, and the price locked at the amount I paid, so that my subscription is immediately active.
11. As a customer with an expired subscription, I want to be able to subscribe again through the same flow, so that I can regain Premium access.
12. As a backend operator, I want the `payments` table schema updated to replace VNPay-specific columns with PayOS-specific ones (order code, PayOS transaction ID, raw webhook payload), so that the audit trail reflects the actual provider.
13. As a developer, I want all VNPay-specific code removed (VNPayClient, VNPayHashHelper, VNPayOptions, the IPN endpoint, renewal scheduler's token-charge logic, VNPay test suites), so that there is no dead code in the codebase.
14. As a developer, I want the payment result service refactored to accept provider-neutral parameters instead of VNPay-specific response fields, so that the subscription activation logic is decoupled from the payment provider.
15. As a backend operator, I want payment orders to expire after 15 minutes, matching the mobile app's QR countdown, so that abandoned payment attempts don't linger as pending indefinitely.
16. As a backend operator, I want the one-pending-per-customer database constraint preserved, so that a customer cannot have two in-flight payment attempts simultaneously.
17. As an admin, I want the existing plan CRUD endpoints (`GET/POST/PATCH /api/admin/subscription-plans`) to continue working unchanged, so that plan management is unaffected by the provider swap.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Provider**: PayOS via the `Net.payOS` NuGet package (official SDK). The SDK's `PayOS` class handles order creation and webhook signature verification. Replaces `IVNPayClient`/`VNPayClient` entirely.
- **New interface**: `IPaymentGateway` wrapping the PayOS SDK - a thin adapter with two methods: `CreateOrderAsync(amount, orderCode, description, expiry, returnUrl, cancelUrl)` returning the QR data string and checkout URL, and `VerifyWebhookSignature(payload, signature)` returning the parsed order result. This is the mockable seam for tests. Registered as a singleton in DI.
- **Configuration**: `PayOSOptions` bound from `configuration.GetSection("PayOS")` with three fields: `ClientId`, `ApiKey`, `ChecksumKey`. Registered via `AddOptions<PayOSOptions>().Bind(...)`. Replaces `VNPayOptions`.
- **Payment entity changes**: The `Payment` entity's VNPay-specific columns (`VnpTxnRef`, `VnpTransactionNo`, `VnpResponseCode`, `VnpTransactionStatus`, `VnpBankCode`, `VnpCardType`, `VnpPayDate`) are replaced with PayOS-specific ones: `OrderCode` (long, unique - PayOS's numeric order identifier), `PayosTransactionId` (string, nullable - PayOS's own transaction reference from the webhook), `RawWebhookPayload` (string, nullable - the full webhook JSON for audit). `IdempotencyKey`, `RawIpnPayload` (renamed to `RawWebhookPayload`), and all non-provider columns (`PaymentId`, `SubscriptionId`, `CustomerId`, `PlanId`, `Amount`, `ChargeType`, `Status`, `PaidAt`, `CreatedAt`, `UpdatedAt`) are unchanged.
- **Migration**: A new Flyway migration drops the VNPay columns, adds the PayOS columns, and updates the unique index from `VnpTxnRef` to `OrderCode`. The one-pending-per-subscription unique partial index is kept.
- **Payment result service**: `ISubscriptionPaymentResultService.ApplyResultAsync` is refactored to accept provider-neutral parameters: `(Payment payment, bool success, string? providerTransactionId, string? rawPayload)`. The subscription creation/renewal logic (initial vs renewal, locked price snapshot, next billing date advancement, idempotent no-op on already-resolved payments, race-condition handling for duplicate active subscriptions) is unchanged - it was already provider-agnostic in substance, just VNPay-shaped in its parameter list.
- **Order code generation**: PayOS requires a numeric `long` order code. Generated as `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.ToUnixTimeMilliseconds() % 1_000_000_000_000` combined with a random suffix, or simply derived from the `PaymentId` GUID's hash. Must be unique; the database unique index on `OrderCode` is the backstop.
- **Endpoints**:
  - `POST /api/subscriptions/create-payment` (authenticated, Customer role): accepts `{ planId, idempotencyKey }`. Creates a `Payment` row with status `pending`, generates the order code, calls `IPaymentGateway.CreateOrderAsync`, returns `{ orderCode, qrCode, amount, expiresAt }`. The `returnUrl`/`cancelUrl` passed to PayOS are backend URLs (informational only since the mobile app renders the QR itself and never opens the checkout URL).
  - `GET /api/subscriptions/payment-status/{orderCode}` (authenticated, Customer role): returns `{ orderCode, status, amount, subscriptionId }`. Ownership-checked (customer can only read their own payments).
  - `POST /api/webhooks/payos` (anonymous): receives PayOS's webhook POST. Verifies the checksum signature via `IPaymentGateway.VerifyWebhookSignature`. Looks up the `Payment` by `OrderCode`. Calls `ApplyResultAsync`. Returns 200 on success (PayOS expects this to stop retrying). Returns 400 on signature failure. Returns 200 even on a duplicate/already-resolved payment (idempotent).
  - `GET /api/subscriptions/plans` and `GET /api/subscriptions/current`: unchanged, already provider-agnostic.
  - `GET /api/subscriptions/vnpay/return` and `GET /api/subscriptions/vnpay/ipn`: deleted.
- **Renewal scheduler**: The existing `SubscriptionRenewalScheduler` (hourly `BackgroundService` that claims due subscriptions and calls `ChargeByTokenAsync`) is removed entirely. PayOS bank transfers are one-time; there is no token-based recurring charge. When a subscription expires, the customer manually re-subscribes through the same create-payment flow. The `AutoRenew`, `NextRetryAt`, `RetryCount`, `RenewalClaimedAt`, `VnpayCardToken` columns on `CustomerSubscription` become unused and can be dropped or left for a follow-up migration.
- **Idempotency**: The mobile app generates an `IdempotencyKey` per checkout attempt. The `create-payment` handler checks for an existing pending payment with that key and returns the same order rather than creating a duplicate. The existing one-pending-per-customer partial unique index provides the database-level backstop.
- **Deleted code**: `VNPayClient`, `VNPayHashHelper`, `VNPayOptions`, `VNPayPaymentRequest`, `ProcessVNPayIpnCommandHandler`, `SubscriptionRenewalScheduler`, the VNPay return endpoint handler, `VNPayCheckoutTests`, `VNPayHashHelperTests`. All references in DI registration removed.

## Testing Decisions

A good test exercises external behavior at the highest available seam. For this feature that means: mock the payment gateway (`IPaymentGateway`) to avoid real PayOS calls, use `TestDbContextFactory` (EF Core in-memory) for database state, and assert on the observable outcome (payment status, subscription existence, HTTP response shape).

### Modules to test

- **Payment result service** (`SubscriptionPaymentResultService`): test via `TestDbContextFactory`. Verify: a pending payment transitions to succeeded and creates a subscription on initial success; a pending payment transitions to failed on failure; a duplicate call on an already-resolved payment is a no-op; the locked price is snapshotted from the payment amount; the next billing date advances by the plan's billing interval. These tests are provider-agnostic (they already were in substance).
- **Create-payment handler**: mock `IPaymentGateway.CreateOrderAsync`, seed a plan in the test DB. Verify: a pending `Payment` row is created with the correct order code and amount; the QR data string is returned; an existing pending payment with the same idempotency key returns the same order; a customer with an active subscription is rejected.
- **Webhook handler**: mock `IPaymentGateway.VerifyWebhookSignature`. Verify: a valid signature + matching order code resolves the payment and creates the subscription; an invalid signature returns 400 and changes nothing; a duplicate webhook for an already-resolved payment returns 200 and changes nothing; an unknown order code returns 200 (PayOS expects 200 even for unrecognized orders to stop retries).
- **Query handlers** (`GetCurrentSubscription`, `GetSubscriptionPayment`): the existing tests are provider-agnostic and carry over with minimal changes (the payment status poll test changes from `paymentId` to `orderCode` lookup).

### Prior art

- `VNPayCheckoutTests` (being replaced) - same `TestDbContextFactory` pattern, same handler-level testing. The new tests follow the same structure.
- `VNPayHashHelperTests` (being replaced) - signature verification tests. The PayOS equivalent tests `IPaymentGateway.VerifyWebhookSignature` with known-good and tampered payloads.
- `AiCategorizationServiceTests`, `BudgetServiceTests` - the established project pattern of mocking interfaces and using `TestDbContextFactory`.

## Out of Scope

- **Feature gating**: deciding which features are premium-only. This spec covers only the payment/subscription activation pipeline.
- **Refunds**: no refund API or admin refund UI. Handled manually outside the system if needed.
- **Auto-renewal / recurring charges**: PayOS bank transfers are one-time. The renewal scheduler is deleted. Customers manually re-subscribe when their plan expires.
- **Dunning / retry logic**: removed along with the renewal scheduler. No automatic retry on failed payments.
- **Email/SMS payment receipts**: no confirmation message sent after payment.
- **Subscription analytics**: no conversion/churn tracking.
- **Admin subscription management UI**: the existing admin plan CRUD is unchanged; no new admin screens.
- **Mobile app changes**: covered by the companion spec (finviet-mobile #91).
- **Dropping the now-unused `CustomerSubscription` renewal columns** (`AutoRenew`, `NextRetryAt`, `RetryCount`, `RenewalClaimedAt`, `VnpayCardToken`): these can be cleaned up in a follow-up migration once the PayOS integration is confirmed working. Not blocking.

## Further Notes

- The `SubscriptionPaymentResultService` is the most valuable piece to preserve through the migration. Its core logic (idempotent payment resolution, initial subscription creation with locked price, renewal advancement, race-condition handling) is already provider-agnostic. The refactoring is limited to its parameter signature.
- PayOS webhook retries: PayOS retries webhooks several times if it doesn't get a 200 response. The handler must return 200 for both successful processing and duplicate/already-resolved payments. Only return non-200 for signature verification failure.
- The `payments` table's `ChargeType` column stays as-is ("initial" / "renewal"), even though renewal via PayOS would be a new "initial" checkout rather than a server-to-server charge. If the renewal scheduler is ever reintroduced with a provider that supports recurring charges, this column is ready.
- The PayOS webhook endpoint is at `/api/webhooks/payos` (not under `/api/subscriptions/`) to match the convention of webhook receivers being at a top-level path. This URL is configured in the PayOS dashboard.
- The existing Flyway migration numbering continues from V0006. The new migration is V0007 or the next available number.

items.title: AEX- OVERVIEW
items.body:
# AEX Web — Developer Onboarding Guide

> This README is a practical, code-verified guide to the `aex-web` codebase (npm package name `bigfixaex`). Every claim below is backed by an exact file path (and line number where useful). Anything that could not be verified from the code is called out explicitly in [Unknowns / Areas Requiring Further Investigation](#unknowns--areas-requiring-further-investigation) instead of being guessed.

---

## Project Overview

**What this project does.** AEX Web is HCL's "Agent Experience" platform: a multi-tenant conversational-AI / chatbot + live-agent-assist web application. A single Node.js/Express server hosts:

- A server-rendered chat widget / bot UI (Handlebars views).
- An **admin/configuration console** (Vue 3 SPA, `src/`) — GenAI agent builder, workflow automation, RBAC, self-heal, learning console, live-agent-console admin, channel configuration, etc.
- A **live-agent console** (Vue 3 SPA, `src-agent/`) — the human-agent chat/dashboard UI used for live chat hand-off.
- A large library of **GenAI/LLM integrations** (Azure OpenAI, OpenAI cloud, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex/Gemini, custom LLM endpoints) plus an **A2A (Agent-to-Agent) protocol** server/client.
- A **Microsoft Bot Framework** connector layer (Teams, Slack, Telegram, Facebook, SMS, email, IVR/Twilio, Google Chat).
- ~50 pluggable **"tool" connectors** (Slack, ServiceNow, Salesforce, Jira, AWS/Azure/GCP services, databases, etc.) that GenAI agents can call as functions.
- Real-time features (live chat, agent transfer, workflow monitoring) over **Socket.IO**.

**Main purpose.** Let enterprise customers (tenants) configure and run AI-powered chatbots and live-agent-assist workflows across many channels, backed by a common admin console, RBAC, and a large set of external-system connectors.

**Main technologies/frameworks:**
- **Backend:** Node.js 24 (pinned in `package.json:205`, enforced at runtime in `app.js:5-8`), Express 4, Express-Handlebars, Socket.IO 4, Passport (LDAP/SAML/OIDC/IBM AppID), Redis (`redis`/`@redis/client`, standalone or cluster), MongoDB / IBM Cloudant / DynamoDB (pluggable via a "Dispatcher" abstraction), `botbuilder` (MS Bot Framework), `@a2a-js/sdk`.
- **Frontend:** Vue 3 + Vue Router + Pinia, built with Vite; two separate SPAs (`src/`, `src-agent/`) plus legacy jQuery/Materialize-based assets under `public/`.
- **Cloud SDKs:** AWS (`@aws-sdk/*`), Azure (`@azure/*`), IBM Cloud (`ibm-cos-sdk`, `@ibm-cloud/cloudant`, `ibmcloud-appid`).
- **Testing:** Vitest.
- **CI/CD:** Azure DevOps pipelines under `DevOps/` (SonarQube, Mend SCA, AppScan SAST, container security, image signing) — see `DevOps/README.md`.

---

## Project Structure

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `app.js` | The entire Express/Socket.IO app bootstrap (see [Application Startup Flow](#application-startup-flow)). |
| `dev.js` / `config-back.js` | `dev.js` hardcodes the local-dev tenant subdomain (`devplayground`). `config-back.js` is a **legacy/unused** Cloudant+Memcache config module, not read by current startup code. |
| `lib/helper/envConfiguration.js` | Loads all configuration and secrets (per-`AEX_ENV`), and creates the global `redisClient`. |
| `lib/corearchitecture.js` | Base class (`CoreArchitecture`) for per-session conversation handling; the canonical example of the `GLOBAL.Dispatcher` service-locator pattern. |
| `lib/scripts/dispatchers/` | The pluggable-backend abstraction layer: DB (`dbServices/`), GenAI (`cognitiveServices/`), object storage (`objectStorageServices/`), key vault, third-party/channel-dependent services. |
| `lib/scripts/` (everything else) | Business-logic modules: live-agent transfer/queueing, bot connectors, A2A protocol, GenAI prompting, workflows, notifications, LDAP client/sync, translation, etc. See [Core Modules](#core-modules). |
| `lib/socket/` | Socket.IO event handlers: `chat.js` (entry point), `liveAgentv2.js` (live-agent broker events), `notification.js`, `workflowMonitor.js`. |
| `routes/` | All HTTP routes, split into `unauthroutes.js` → `naclroutes.js` → `aclroutes.js` (mounted in that order — see [Application Architecture](#application-architecture)), plus ~40 feature subfolders (`genAI/`, `liveAgentConsole/`, `rbac/`, `lums/`, `channels/`, `workflows/`, etc.). |
| `middleware/` | `ldapRoleRefresh.js` (background LDAP role sync) and `rbac/` (permission middleware, static role/permission matrix, user-operation guards). |
| `models/` | Data-access classes. Either extend `models/base/index.js` (`BaseModel`, wraps the Dispatcher), call the Dispatcher directly (legacy prototype style, e.g. `models/customer.js`), or are pure-Redis models (e.g. `models/webNotifications.js`). |
| `tools/` | ~50 self-contained connector plugins (Slack, ServiceNow, AWS, databases, etc.) with a uniform `{name, fields, functions[]}` shape, invocable as LLM function-calling tools. |
| `src/` | Vue 3 SPA — the **admin/configuration console**, served at `/admin`. |
| `src-agent/` | Vue 3 SPA — the **live-agent console** (chat + live dashboard), served at `/agents`. |
| `views/` | Handlebars templates — legacy/auth pages, the server-rendered chat widget, login/SSO/OIDC pages. |
| `public/` | Static assets, including the legacy embeddable chat-widget bundle (built by `buildEngine/bundle.js`). |
| `buildEngine/` | Build/post-build tooling: `uiCacher.js` (Brotli-compresses & uploads `dist/` to object storage/CDN after `vite build`), `bundle.js` (legacy chat-widget bundler). |
| `config/` | Only `config/actions.js` exists in this checkout (a small action-name registry). `config/config.js` (the local/dev default config) is referenced by code but **not present** in this checkout — see [Unknowns](#unknowns--areas-requiring-further-investigation). |
| `migrate/` | **Tenant provisioning** scripts (`core.js`, `manage.js`) — not a schema-migration framework; seeds new-tenant data (users, views, default groups, console catalog). |
| `tests/` | Vitest test suite, mirrors `routes/`, `lib/`, `models/`, `middleware/` structure. |
| `tools*/DevOps/deployment` config | `Dockerfile` (root), `deployment/{dev,ibm,onprem}/` (per-environment Dockerfiles/build scripts), `DevOps/` (CI pipeline YAMLs + its own README). |

---

## Application Architecture

```
                                   ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                                   │   Browser / External Client │
                                   └───────────────┬─────────────┘
                                                    │ HTTPS
                     ┌──────────────────────────────┼──────────────────────────────┐
                     │                              │                              │
             GET /admin (SPA)               GET /agents (SPA)              GET / , /login, bots,
             src/ (Vue3, Pinia)             src-agent/ (Vue3, Pinia)       channels, APIs, webhooks
                     │                              │                              │
                     └──────────────┬───────────────┴───────────────┬──────────────┘
                                    ▼                                ▼
                    ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                    │                     Express app (app.js)                  │
                    │  session (connect-redis) → tenant/subdomain resolve →     │
                    │  unauthroutes.js → naclroutes.js → aclroutes.js → 404     │
                    │  RBAC: middleware/rbac/*  |  LDAP refresh: ldapRoleRefresh │
                    └───────────────┬───────────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                                    │                        │
                     ┌──────────────▼───────────┐   ┌────────▼─────────────────┐
                     │   Socket.IO (default ns)  │   │  GLOBAL.Dispatcher       │
                     │  chat.js → liveAgentv2.js,│   │  (service locator)       │
                     │  workflowMonitor.js,       │   │  .DB   → Mongo/Cloudant/ │
                     │  notification.js           │   │          DynamoDB       │
                     │  (@socket.io/redis-adapter │   │  .CGS  → GenAI providers│
                     │   for multi-instance pub/  │   │  .OSS  → object storage │
                     │   sub via redisClient)      │   │  .KP,.TPA,.CDS → more   │
                     └──────────────┬───────────┘   └────────┬─────────────────┘
                                    │                         │
                     ┌──────────────▼──────────────┐  ┌───────▼────────────────────┐
                     │  lib/scripts/* business logic│  │  models/* (BaseModel or    │
                     │  agentManager, queueManager, │  │  direct Dispatcher calls)  │
                     │  transferManager, agentTransfer,│└───────┬────────────────────┘
                     │  connectorBots (Bot Framework),│         │
                     │  a2aServer/a2aClient, workflows,│         ▼
                     │  ldapClient/ldapSync, gptPrompter│  MongoDB / Cloudant / DynamoDB
                     └──────────────┬──────────────┘   (system of record, per DB_TYPE)
                                    │
                     ┌──────────────▼──────────────┐
                     │        tools/* (~50)         │
                     │  Slack, ServiceNow, AWS, DBs, │
                     │  webhooks... invoked as LLM   │
                     │  function-calling tools        │
                     └───────────────────────────────┘

                     Redis (global `redisClient`, standalone or cluster):
                     sessions (connect-redis) · caching (lib/helper/caching.js) ·
                     rate limiting · Socket.IO adapter pub/sub · agent/queue/transfer
                     state · LDAP connection-pool invalidation · A2A context cache
```

Key architectural traits:
- **Single global service locator** (`GLOBAL.Dispatcher`, set once in `app.js:181`) hides which physical backend (Mongo/Cloudant/DynamoDB, which GenAI provider, which object-storage vendor) answers a given call — see [Database / Storage](#database--storage).
- **Global singletons via bare `GLOBAL`/`config`/`redisClient`/`passport` variables** (declared `writable` via ESLint globals in `.eslintrc.cjs:13-20`), not passed through constructors/DI — an important non-obvious convention for new contributors.
- **Three route "tiers"** (`unauthroutes.js` → `naclroutes.js` → `aclroutes.js`) implement a coarse-grained "must be logged in" / "no ACL" / "ACL + RBAC" split, layered with a finer-grained RBAC v2 permission system (`middleware/rbac/`).
- **Two independent Vue SPAs** (`src/` admin console, `src-agent/` agent console) are built as **separate Vite entry points** (`vite.config.js:27-40`: `index.html` → `main`, `agent.html` → `agent`) and served from the same Express server at `/admin` and `/agents` respectively.
- **Redis is load-bearing infrastructure**, not just a cache: sessions, Socket.IO horizontal scaling (via `@socket.io/redis-adapter`), live-agent queue/transfer state, rate limiting, and LDAP pool coordination all depend on it.

---

## Application Startup Flow

Entry point: `npm start` → `node app.js` (`package.json:12`).

1. **Node version gate** — `app.js:5-8` exits immediately if the running Node isn't v24.x.
2. **`require('module-alias/register')`** (`app.js:9`) activates the `_moduleAliases` map from `package.json:209-219` (`@root`, `@models`, `@lib`, `@libscr`, `@libhlp`, `@helpers`, `@routes`, `@tools`, `@middleware`) so every subsequent `require('@lib/...')`-style import resolves correctly.
3. **`initEnv()`** — `require('@libhlp/envConfiguration').init` (i.e. `lib/helper/envConfiguration.js`) is awaited **before anything else runs**. This:
   - Builds the global `config` object from `process.env.AEX_ENV` (`aks` | `eks` | `onprem` | default) — see [Configuration](#configuration).
   - In production, fetches secrets from the environment's secret store (Azure Key Vault for `aks`, AWS Secrets Manager/IAM for `eks`, OpenBao for `onprem`).
   - Creates the global `redisClient` — a Redis Cluster client (`@redis/client` `createCluster`) or standalone client (`createClient`) depending on `config.IS_REDIS_CLUSTER_MODE`, connects it, and PINGs it before returning.
4. Inside the `.then(async () => {...})` callback (the rest of `app.js`):
   - Express app + `http.createServer(app)` + Socket.IO server (`new IOServer(server, {pingTimeout:15000, serveClient:false})`) are created (`app.js:12-26`).
   - Handlebars view engine registered with custom `json`/`checkif` helpers (`app.js:34-52`).
   - **Session store**: `connect-redis`'s `RedisStore` wraps `redisClient` (`app.js:54-56`); cookie name `app`; secure/`sameSite:'none'`/`partitioned` cookies in production.
   - Body parsers, `passport.initialize()/session()`, `connect-flash`, `lusca` security headers (nosniff, HSTS, CSP, referrer-policy), `morgan` logging (`app.js:99-149`).
   - **`GLOBAL` wiring** (`init()`, `app.js:179-198`): `GLOBAL.TEMP_PATH`, `GLOBAL.Dispatcher = new (require('./lib/scripts/dispatchers'))()`, `GLOBAL.SplitIntent`, and `require('./lib/scripts/translationAgent').translationInit()`.
   - **Tenant/subdomain resolution middleware** (`app.js:202-235`): from `config.SUB_DOMAIN` for on-prem/aks/eks, or parsed from `req.hostname` for multi-tenant SaaS (session destroyed on subdomain mismatch); `dev.js`'s hardcoded subdomain is used outside production.
   - **`@socket.io/redis-adapter` wiring** (`app.js:164-171`): duplicates `redisClient` into a `sub` client, then `io.adapter(createAdapter(redisClient, sub, {...}))` — this is what lets Socket.IO events fan out across multiple app instances.
   - **Route mounting**, strictly in this order (`app.js:238-243`): `unauthroutes.js` → `naclroutes.js` → `aclroutes.js` → 404 handler.
   - **`startServer(port, address)`** (`app.js:268-277`) polls `vectorDBs('checkConnection')` every second and only calls `server.listen(...)` once the vector DB connection is confirmed. Production listens on `process.env.PORT` at `0.0.0.0`; non-production hardcodes port `3000` on `localhost`.
   - Graceful-shutdown handlers (`SIGINT`/`SIGTERM`/etc., production only) decrement Redis-backed agent-queue counters and close Redis/vector-DB connections before `process.exit`.
   - Finally, `lib/socket/chat.js` and `lib/socket/notification.js` are initialized with `io` and the duplicated `sub` Redis client (`app.js:334-335`) — this is where the single `io.on('connection', ...)` handler actually lives (see [Request/API Flow](#requestapi-flow)).

## Request/API Flow

### HTTP request path
```
Client
  → app.js middleware chain (cookies, session/RedisStore, tenant-subdomain resolve,
     body parsers, passport, lusca security headers, morgan)
  → routes/unauthroutes.js   (public: assets, /login, /logout, captcha, webhooks, bot inbound...)
       → ends with a login gate: if !req.session.username → redirect to '/' (unless XHR/API)
  → routes/naclroutes.js     (must be logged in; ldapRoleRefresh middleware; e.g. /agent, /notify, /user_info)
  → routes/aclroutes.js      (admin/management; re-validates customer_credentials; legacy v1 ACL check;
                               RBAC v2 via routes/permissionWrappers.js + middleware/rbac/permissionMiddleware.js)
  → route handler (routes/**/index.js)
       → models/* (BaseModel-backed, legacy-prototype, or pure-Redis)
            → GLOBAL.Dispatcher.service(GLOBAL.Dispatcher.DB, serviceKeys) → Mongo/Cloudant/DynamoDB
       → and/or lib/scripts/* business logic (agentTransfer, workflows, gptPrompter, connectorBots...)
       → and/or redisClient directly (cache, queue counters, rate limiting)
  → res.json(...) / res.render(...) / res.send(...)   (no centralized error-formatting helper — see Error Handling)
```

### Real example — `GET /admin/agentassist/desk/:title` (fetch a live-agent "desk")
1. `app.js:243` mounts `aclroutes.js`.
2. `routes/aclroutes.js:62` — `router.use('/admin', csrfLoginCheck, require('./admin.js'))`.
3. `routes/admin.js:85` — `router.use(adminLogger)` (writes an `AdminLog` audit record for every admin request).
4. `routes/admin.js:113` — `registerRouteWithPermission(router, '/agentassist', require('./liveAgentConsole'))` (from `routes/permissionWrappers.js`) inserts `hasPermission('agentAssist','view')` before mounting.
5. `routes/liveAgentConsole/index.js:11` — `router.use('/desk', require('./desks'))`.
6. `routes/liveAgentConsole/desks/index.js:18-21` — `router.get('/:title', isUserAdmin, async (req,res) => { ... })`; `isUserAdmin` (`desks/index.js:62-69`) restricts to `Admin`/`Viewer` roles via `@libhlp/agentUtility`.
7. Handler calls `new Desk(req.session).get(req.params.title)` (a `BaseModel`-backed model) and responds `res.json({deskDetails})`.

### Real example — `GET /notify/fetchNotifications`
1. `app.js:240` mounts `naclroutes.js`; `naclroutes.js:98` — `router.use('/notify', require('./pushNotification.js').auth)`.
2. `routes/pushNotification.js:40-47` — `router.get('/fetchNotifications', ...)` builds a range key from `req.session.username`, instantiates `new Notification({}, req.session)` (`models/pushNotification.js`), and returns raw DB docs via `res.send(data)`.

### Socket.IO event path (live agent chat)
```
Client socket connects (query.agent=true from src-agent/) 
  → lib/socket/chat.js: single io.on('connection', ...) handler (app.js:334 wires this in)
       → chat.js:492 detects query.agent and skips end-user chatbot listeners
       → chat.js:523 calls AgentTransferSocketEvents(socket)  (== lib/socket/liveAgentv2.js's init())
            → liveAgentv2.js registers 'Transfer Broker' / 'Agent Broker' / 'Peer Broker' / 'disconnect'
            → each Broker event's payload carries an internal `event` name dispatched via switch
            → handlers use QueueManager / AgentManager / TransferManager (all backed by redisClient)
              and lib/scripts/agentTransfer (desk queueing, transfer orchestration, models/agentAssist/*)
```
